{{short description|American cell biologist (born 1932)}}

'''Daniel Branton''' (born January 13, 1932) is an American cell biologist. He is the Higgins Professor of Biology, Emeritus at [[Harvard University]]. His research has played a key role in visualizing the composition of the cell membrane and later in the development of DNA [[nanopore sequencing]]. <ref name="harvardmcbprofile" />

Branton earned a Bachelor of Arts in mathematics at [[Cornell University]], then moved to the [[University of California, Berkeley]] to pursue a PhD in plant physiology.<ref name="nasprofile"/> He taught at UC–Berkeley until joining the [[Harvard University]] faculty in 1973,<ref name="nasprofile"/> where he later held the Higgins Professorship of Biology.<ref name="harvardmcbprofile">{{cite news |title=Daniel Branton |url=https://www.mcb.harvard.edu/directory/daniel-branton/ |access-date=25 April 2025 |publisher=Harvard University Department of Molecular and Cellular Biology}}</ref> In 1985, Branton was president of the [[American Society for Cell Biology]].<ref>{{cite news |title=ASCB Presidents |url=https://www.ascb.org/about-ascb/presidents/ |access-date=25 April 2025 |publisher=American Society for Cell Biology}}</ref>

He won a [[Guggenheim Fellowship]] in 1970,<ref name="gfprofile">{{cite news |title=Daniel Branton |url=https://www.gf.org/fellows/daniel-branton/ |access-date=25 April 2025 |publisher=John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation}}</ref> and was elected to membership within the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] and the [[United States National Academy of Sciences]] in 1974 and 1981, respectively.<ref name="nasprofile">{{cite news |title=Daniel Branton Harvard University |url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/daniel-branton-a6kpyw/ |access-date=25 April 2025 |publisher=United States National Academy of Sciences}}</ref><ref name="amacadprofile">{{cite news |title=Professor Daniel Branton |url=https://www.amacad.org/person/daniel-branton |access-date=25 April 2025 |publisher=American Academy of Arts and Sciences}}</ref>
